author: Claude (English teacher role)
basis: Replaces the original B1 column of sheet 'SDG 13-1' (48.4 words per slide, all 20 slides over the 20-second limit). Facts unchanged: Climate Change Response Act, Net Zero 2050, carbon fee, offshore wind, Silicon Shield, smart grids, carbon capture, swappable batteries, greenwashing, the nuclear/gas debate. Band: 32-40 words, 11-16 words per sentence, FK 7-11, speakable in 20 s.

slides.1: Have you noticed that our summers keep getting longer and hotter? This is not your imagination, because our world is facing a real climate crisis. Today I will show you how we fight it.
slides.2: So what is SDG 13? It is a global call for climate action, and it asks every country to cut carbon and prepare for disasters. The goal is to keep our planet cool.
slides.3: Now think about Taiwan. As a small island, we are easily hurt by typhoons and rising seas, and our high-tech factories use huge amounts of energy. Can we still lead in green energy?
slides.4: The data is worrying, because Taiwan is warming faster than the global average. This changes everything, from the food we grow to the water we drink. Record heatwaves may soon become normal.
slides.5: Here is the main problem. Taiwan still depends on coal and gas, which produce a lot of carbon, while our chip industry needs power every hour. Can we grow and cut pollution together?
slides.6: We have to ask some difficult questions. Is this high-energy lifestyle really sustainable, and can we move to green power fast enough? Students and scientists like us have to answer them.
slides.7: But there is good news. Taiwan has passed the Climate Change Response Act, which sets one clear goal: Net Zero by 2050. Companies that pollute more now pay a higher carbon fee.
slides.8: Our landscape has changed as well. Offshore wind turbines now stand in the Taiwan Strait, and our wind power is growing quickly. Solar panels have also appeared on school and factory roofs.
slides.9: People here recycle carefully, and we use the MRT and Ubike more than ever, so green living has become popular. However, recycling alone is not enough to stop the crisis.
slides.10: How can technology help us? Taiwan is building smart grids that use artificial intelligence to manage electricity. Imagine a brain that knows exactly where power is needed; this cuts a lot of waste.
slides.11: Another innovation is carbon capture. Scientists here catch carbon dioxide from factory chimneys before it reaches the air, and then store it safely underground. It sounds impossible, but it already works.
slides.12: Think about our streets, where Taiwan is famous for electric scooters with swappable batteries. This clever design reduces both pollution and noise in crowded cities, and other countries are copying it.
slides.13: However, going green is not easy, because new technology is expensive and many small businesses worry about the cost. If we are not careful, climate policy will leave poorer families behind.
slides.14: Energy security is another serious debate. Our high-tech industry needs stable power day and night, but wind and solar depend on the weather. Should we choose nuclear power or more natural gas?
slides.15: Climate change is a global fight, so Taiwan wants to share its technology with other countries. International politics makes this difficult, but a storm in one country affects all of us.
slides.16: Finally, we must stay careful about greenwashing, which happens when companies look green but never really change. As students, we should check the data and ask whether promises are actually kept.
slides.17: To sum up, Taiwan is on the right track. We now have the laws, the wind power and the smart technology. We are slowly becoming a green leader instead of a carbon-heavy island.
slides.18: Why does this matter to you? Because you are the future scientists and leaders who can use STEM to invent better solutions. You can also start today by saving energy and speaking up.
slides.19: Do not feel overwhelmed by the climate crisis; feel motivated instead. Taiwan has the talent and the determination to lead this change. Let us build a country with clean air and blue skies.
slides.20: The clock is ticking and the Earth is calling for action, so will you be part of the solution? Taiwan is ready for SDG 13, and so am I. Let us start together now.
